- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.4), model often overshoots upward; cap upward revisions at +1.5–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile or mixed; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 0.5–1.5 units.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ units in 3–5 days), model often overreacts with sustained overforecasting; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 unit per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.3–0.7 units to forecast to align with recent mean.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag in recognizing downward momentum; shift forecast 1–2 days earlier to match sentiment trend.
